title: Which states require human trafficking training for licensed health professionals?
description: State human trafficking training for licensed health professionals as at November 2026: Texas HB 2059 and Florida 456.0341 and 464.013 by profession.
shortAnswer: Several US states make human trafficking training a condition of health professional licensure. Texas House Bill 2059 (2019) requires licensed health care practitioners who provide direct patient care, including physicians and nurses, to complete a course approved by the Health and Human Services Commission, for renewals from September 1, 2020. Florida section 456.0341 required a one-time 1 hour course by January 1, 2021 for physicians, pharmacists, dentists and other listed professions, while Florida nurses complete 2 hours every biennium.
keyTakeaways: Texas HB 2059 took effect September 1, 2019 and added Occupations Code chapter 116 for most health care practitioners, section 156.060 for physicians and section 301.308 for nurses.
Texas courses must be approved by the Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC), which must offer at least one free course and revised its review standards in March 2025.
Frequency differs by Texas board: nurses every licensing period, physicians in the first renewal period and every third renewal after that, and pharmacists as a renewal reporting condition.
Florida section 456.0341 required a one-time 1 hour course by January 1, 2021 for listed professions, and a workplace sign in English and Spanish by January 1, 2025.
Florida nurses must complete a separate 2 hour course for every biennial renewal on or after January 1, 2019, even if exempt from other CE through specialty certification.
regulator: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) with the Texas Medical Board, Texas Board of Nursing and Texas State Board of Pharmacy; Florida Department of Health and its professional boards
appliesTo: Texas health care practitioners licensed under Occupations Code title 3 who provide direct patient care, including physicians, nurses and pharmacists
Florida physicians, osteopathic physicians, chiropractors, podiatrists, optometrists, pharmacists, dentists, massage therapists, physical therapists and other professions listed in section 456.0341
Florida registered nurses, licensed practical nurses and certified nursing assistants regulated under chapter 464
Hospitals, clinics, pharmacies and staffing agencies that track license renewal compliance

sections.heading: Why do states require human trafficking training for health professionals?

blocks.text: States require it because health professionals may encounter trafficking victims in clinical settings, and licensure renewal is a lever states already control. The laws differ in who is covered, how long the course is, whether it repeats, and who approves content, so a multistate employer cannot apply one rule to all staff.

This page covers Texas and Florida, the two states named most often in compliance questions, using the statutes and board rules themselves. Other states have their own requirements, which should be checked with each licensing board before a multistate program is finalized.

[Texas House Bill 2059](https://capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/86R/billtext/html/HB02059F.htm), passed by the 86th Legislature and effective September 1, 2019, requires licensed health care practitioners who provide direct patient care to complete a human trafficking prevention course approved by the executive commissioner of HHSC. It created three routes in the Occupations Code.

items: **Chapter 116:** a "health care practitioner" is an individual licensed under title 3 to engage in a health care profession who provides direct patient care. Practitioners other than physicians and nurses must complete an approved course as a condition of license renewal, and were not required to comply before September 1, 2020.

**Section 156.060 (physicians):** a physician designating a direct patient care practice must complete an approved course as part of required CME, and the Texas Medical Board must designate it as medical ethics or professional responsibility credit.
**Section 301.308 (nurses):** a nurse who provides direct patient care must complete an approved course as part of the continuing competency program.

blocks.text: Sections 156.060 and 301.308 apply to physician registration and nursing license renewals on or after September 1, 2020. Section 116.002(b) requires HHSC to approve courses, including at least one available without charge, and to post the list on its website.

blocks.title: Occupations Code 116.002(a), as enacted
blocks.text: "A health care practitioner, other than a physician or nurse, within the time prescribed by commission rule shall successfully complete a training course approved by the executive commissioner on identifying and assisting victims of human trafficking."

sections.heading: How often must Texas physicians, nurses and pharmacists complete the course?

blocks.text: Each Texas board applies its own frequency. The [Texas Medical Board](https://www.tmb.texas.gov/apply-renew/physician/continuing-education-requirements-for-physicians) requires physicians in direct patient care to complete at least 1 hour in the first renewal period after licensure and at least 1 hour every third renewal period after that, about every six years, with HHSC approved courses counting toward the 2 hour ethics or professional responsibility requirement.

The [Texas Board of Nursing](https://www.bon.texas.gov/education_continuing_education.asp.html) requires nurses who provide direct patient care to complete an HHSC approved course before the end of every licensing period, for renewals on or after September 1, 2020. Certification cannot substitute, and the board notes that HHSC revised its course review standards in March 2025 and is reviewing all courses, including those previously approved. Details are in [Texas nursing continuing education](/regulations/texas-nursing-continuing-education).

For pharmacists, [22 Texas Administrative Code section 295.8](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/22-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-295-8) makes completion of the course required by Occupations Code section 116.002 part of the renewal reporting requirements. HHSC's [health care practitioner human trafficking training page](https://www.hhs.texas.gov/services/safety/texas-human-trafficking-resource-center/health-care-practitioner-human-trafficking-training) lists approved courses, including its free HEART training for direct service health care providers.

[Section 456.0341, Florida Statutes](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0456/Sections/0456.0341.html), required each covered licensee or certificate holder to complete a board approved, or department approved where there is no board, 1 hour continuing education course on human trafficking by January 1, 2021. The course must address sex trafficking and labor trafficking, how to identify possible victims, how to report cases, and resources for victims.

It applies to people licensed under chapters 457 (acupuncture), 458 (medicine), 459 (osteopathic medicine), 460 (chiropractic), 461 (podiatric medicine), 463 (optometry), 465 (pharmacy), 466 (dentistry), 480 (massage therapy) and 486 (physical therapy), and parts II, III, V and X of chapter 468. Boards must count the hour within the profession's total required CE hours.

blocks.title: Workplace sign, due January 1, 2025
blocks.text: Covered licensees must post, in a conspicuous place accessible to employees, a sign at least 11 by 15 inches in at least 32 point type, in English and Spanish, giving the Florida Human Trafficking Hotline, 1-855-FLA-SAFE. The requirement was added by chapter 2024-184, Laws of Florida.

Florida nurses follow their own, stricter rule. [Section 464.013(3)(c)](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0464/Sections/0464.013.html) requires every person licensed or certified under chapter 464 to complete a 2 hour course on human trafficking for every biennial licensure renewal on or after January 1, 2019, within the maximum biennial CE hours.

The statute prescribes the content: types of trafficking such as labor and sex and its extent; risk factors; public and private social services for rescue, food, clothing and shelter referrals; hotlines run by the National Human Trafficking Resource Center and the US Department of Homeland Security; validated assessment tools and general indicators; procedures for sharing information with a patient; and referral options for legal and social services. The requirement applies even to nurses exempt from other CE through specialty certification, and the Board of Nursing states the course does not have to be board approved if it meets the statutory criteria. See [Florida nursing continuing education](/regulations/florida-nursing-continuing-education).

blocks.text: The Florida one-time deadline has passed, so new Florida licensees should be checked against current board guidance at their first renewal rather than assumed exempt. Retaining certificates in line with each board's records rule, described in [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit), keeps the evidence usable.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records course approval as part of the obligation, so a Texas requirement is only met by a course on the current HHSC list and a Florida nursing course is checked against the statutory content items. When HHSC re-reviews courses, as it began doing in March 2025, affected records can be flagged together. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Does Texas require human trafficking training for every health care license?
faqs.a: HB 2059 covers individuals licensed under Occupations Code title 3 to engage in a health care profession who provide direct patient care. Physicians and nurses are covered through their own sections, 156.060 and 301.308, and other practitioners through chapter 116. Licensees who do not provide direct patient care fall outside the definition.

faqs.q: Do Texas physicians need human trafficking CE every renewal?
faqs.a: No. The Texas Medical Board requires at least 1 hour in the first renewal period after licensure and at least 1 hour every third renewal period after that, about every six years. The course must be HHSC approved and counts toward the medical ethics or professional responsibility hours.

faqs.q: Is Florida's 1 hour human trafficking course still required?
faqs.a: Section 456.0341 required covered licensees to complete it by January 1, 2021, and required the bilingual workplace sign by January 1, 2025. Florida nurses have a separate, recurring requirement of 2 hours every biennium under section 464.013(3)(c). Licensees should confirm with their board how the one-time course applies to people licensed after 2021.

faqs.q: Is there a free approved course in Texas?
faqs.a: Yes. HB 2059 requires HHSC to approve at least one course available without charge, and HHSC offers its HEART training free online for direct service health care providers and other licensed professionals.
